overall: Tomorrow (Friday, June 26) will be a warm, partly sunny day with a south-southwest flow driving temperatures well above normal into the low-to-mid 90s per NWS. Afternoon convection is a meaningful concern, with a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms developing after 2pm that could briefly cap daytime heating if storms fire early enough. Overall, expect a hot summer day with increasing clouds and storm risk as the afternoon progresses.

The active even-bucket Kalshi market top bucket of 90-91F is well-supported by the ensemble and aligns with the NBM and Weather.com consensus; NWS forecasting 94°F and ECMWF/HRRR running warmer suggest upside risk. Confidence is moderate — the GFS divergence and 40% afternoon storm chance introduce legitimate spread, but the 90-91F even bucket remains the highest-probability single outcome.
